content: The medication homatropine hydrobromide is used primarily before eye examinations (such as refraction), before and after certain eye surgeries, and to treat specific eye conditions like uveitis. It belongs to a class of drugs known as anticholinergics. To apply the eye drops, first wash your hands thoroughly. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using the drops. Tilt your head back, look upward, and gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pouch. Hold the dropper directly above your eye and place one drop into the pouch. Look downward and gently close your eyes for 1-2 minutes. Avoid blinking or rubbing your eye. Do not rinse the dropper, and replace the cap after each use. If you are using other eye medications (such as drops or ointments), wait at least 5-10 minutes before applying them. If this medication is prescribed on a regular schedule, use it consistently at the same times each day to maximize its benefits. Common side effects may include burning, stinging, redness of the eye, irritation, or temporary blurred vision. These effects are usually mild and temporary. However, if you experience severe or persistent symptoms, contact your doctor. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. If you notice signs of an allergic reaction, such as rash, itching, swelling, severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek medical attention immediately. Before using homatropine hydrobromide, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, to belladonna alkaloids (such as atropine), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. After applying the medication, your vision may become temporarily blurred, and your eyes may be more sensitive to light. Protect your eyes in bright light. Infants and small children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug. Avoid allowing the medication to enter a child’s mouth. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, and it is unknown if it passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may be harmful if swallowed. In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention. In the U.S., call 911 or the Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222. In Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. If you miss a dose and are using this medication on a regular schedule, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze it. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
